CMVS / ITEE, University of Oulu, Oulu, Finland University Profile

I am a doctoral researcher at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE), University of Oulu, specialising in artificial intelligence and remote sensing for hydrology modelling. My work focuses on developing deep learning methods that extract snow and water characteristics from multi-modal satellite imagery — combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and DEM data to build climate-resilient runoff prediction models.

My academic journey spans multiple continents: a BSc and MSc in electrical engineering and communication systems from Bahir Dar University, Ethiopia, followed by an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree (IPCV) across the University of Bordeaux (France), Autonomous University of Madrid (Spain), and Pázmány Péter Catholic University (Hungary). Research visits to RISE Sweden (Gothenburg) and University of Florida TREC have broadened my expertise to Nordic snow monitoring and multi-sensor tropical remote sensing.

Presented CrossFuse — a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture for fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical data for high-resolution snow cover estimation — at the Digital Waters Flagship Biannual Meeting, Aalto University, Espoo, Finland. Paper coming soon.

Co-organised the HydroImaging workshop — "Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling" — accepted at IEEE ICIP 2026, Tampere, Finland (Sep 13–17, 2026). Keynote by Prof. Kevin Tansey (University of Leicester).

Computer vision system for automated protozoan disease detection using a custom-built microscopy platform. Achieves real-time classification of blood-borne pathogens, reducing diagnostic time in resource-limited clinical settings. Awarded Best Project, Bahir Dar University 2018 and Best 50 African Projects, Africa Innovation Week 2019.

University of Oulu — ITEE Faculty, Oulu, Finland. Developing AI-driven methods for satellite image processing to determine snow water characteristics. Integrating Sentinel-1/2 with deep learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow) for hydrological modelling. Co-organising HydroImaging Workshop at IEEE ICIP 2026. Funded doctoral position.

University of Oulu, Finland. Established data processing pipelines for hydrological parameter estimation. Developed novel deep learning models for snow-cloud segmentation achieving breakthrough accuracy with the mDeepLabV3+ architecture.

University of Florida TREC, Gainesville, FL, USA

PhD in AI and Remote Sensing Technology for Hydrology Modelling

University of Oulu, Faculty of ITEE, Oulu, Finland. Research focus: deep learning frameworks for snow hydrology parameter estimation using Earth observation data.

Master's Degree

IPCV Excellence Scholarship Master's Degree

Bahir Dar University, Bahir Dar, Ethiopia. Advanced study in signal processing, communication systems, digital image processing, and computer vision fundamentals.
